notes:
DELIVERABLE: reproducible stochastic whole-cohort generator returning exactly 3,000 complete equal-weight fictional records, not reconstructed individuals. This is one explicitly assumed transport scenario for the requested weighted laboratory-substudy complete-case analytical population; no claim to reproduce its actual distribution, weights, selection, or national representativeness. No excluded-study measurements or results were retrieved or used. Screening is conservative. ELIGIBILITY: age 20-79 and sex coding enforced. Rows are interpreted as eligible non-reported-pregnant adults with admissible baseline anthropometry/BP and positive finite laboratory weight; pregnancy, individual weights, HbA1c, and medication are not output or used for restriction. Unknown/inapplicable pregnancy is not separately identifiable or excluded. There is no diabetes, treatment, or hypertension selection. Equal-weight rows approximate a hypothetical already-weighted distribution, not a survey sample with design weights.
EVIDENCE: (1) Moura et al., Braz J Med Biol Res 2020, DOI 10.1590/1414-431X20209815, PMC7433850, full text Study sample/Study variables and Table 1. Baseline 2008-2010, 15,085 Brazilian civil servants, 35-74, six cities, complete BMI/neck/waist measurements; 54.4% female. Table 1 gives sex-specific marginal means/SDs used verbatim in source_moments. All hypertension/diabetes statuses are present; these are not untreated or healthy-only summaries. Height/weight measured, BMI kg/m^2. BP mmHg, seated after >=5 minutes rest, three readings one minute apart, mean last two. Civil-servant selection, source age restriction and complete-anthropometry selection do not identify the user's distribution. (2) Dyer et al., 'Body mass index versus height and weight in relation to blood pressure. Findings for the 10,079 persons in the INTERSALT Study', 1990, PMID2180281, DOI10.1093/oxfordjournals.aje.a115543, full abstract read. 10,079 men/women 20-59, 52 centers, standardized protocol. Reported BMI partial correlations are 0.215 for SBP and 0.229 for DBP with adjustment for age, sex, alcohol, smoking and sodium/potassium excretion. These are partial correlations, NOT slopes and NOT SBP-DBP residual correlation; transfer to an age/sex-only model is explicitly assumed. (3) 'The INTERSALT study: relations of body mass index to blood pressure', 1989, PMID2810326, full abstract read: corroborates positive within-center BMI relationships and similar coefficients at20-39/40-59; its 3.0/2.2 mmHg per10kg WEIGHT summary is not used as a BMI slope. These two INTERSALT publications share participants and are not independent replications. A Copenhagen uric-acid paper was retrieved but not used for any parameter.
DERIVED MODEL: Build a discrete maximum-entropy ELSA reference age PMF on35..74 matching each sex's reported age mean/SD (quadratic exponential family). Define assumed age curves g for BMI and h for BP. BMI conditional mean is ELSA sex mean+g(a)-E_source[g], and conditional variance equals ELSA BMI variance-Var_source[g]. Use shifted lognormal BMI with floor12, positive right skew and constant conditional variance. For each BP, derive a common BMI slope b in mmHg per1kg/m^2 by the positive root of (V_BMI_res/r^2+V_g)b^2+2Cov(h,g)b+V_h-V_BP=0, pooling within-sex variances with source female fraction. Then derive sex-specific pressure innovation variances to reproduce the ELSA sex-specific marginal BP SDs before safety rejection. Conditional BP means are source BP mean+h(a)-E_source[h]+b*(BMI-source BMI mean). Thus published marginal SDs are not incorrectly treated as residual SDs. This algebra is a cross-study synthetic constraint, not a fitted Brazilian regression. Slopes per5 are5b; actual finite-sample regressions need not equal5b, particularly for misspecified linear age adjustment.
UNSUPPORTED ASSUMPTIONS: Target age-band probabilities20s..70s=.23,.22,.20,.17,.12,.06, uniform integer ages within bands; sex probabilities by band=.52,.53,.54,.55,.56,.58. They are scenario choices, not measured target demographics and not copied from the selected civil-servant source. Smooth/hockey-stick age functions, no BMI-by-sex or BMI-by-age slope interaction, source moment transport, shifted-lognormal BMI, and homoscedastic-within-sex Gaussian pressure innovations are assumptions. SBP age slopes .50 men/.75 women with extra .10 after55; DBP slopes .18/.20, diminished by .55 after55; BMI slope .07 with -.004*(age-55)_+^2. They encode plausible widening pulse pressure/late DBP decline but were not estimated in the retrieved papers. SBP-DBP conditional innovation Pearson rho=.65 is an explicit unsupported dependence assumption, NOT an external estimate. Sensitivity runs changing residual_rho (e.g. .45/.80) are important for analysis3. Fixed parameters do not include calibrated epidemiologic/transport uncertainty; seed variation is individual sampling variability only.
MEASUREMENT: Outputs represent observed baseline final-interview BP on an ELSA-like rested seated mean-of-last-two scale. Actual released final-reading aggregation is unspecified, so do not assert it is that protocol or an error-free usual BP. Correlated innovations jointly include physiology, unmeasured treatment/comorbidity and encounter/device error; no separate measurement-error variance or correction can be identified. Laboratory eligibility does not move BP timing to the later blood draw. No rounding to integer pressures or invented replicate readings. BP pairs are jointly rejection-sampled only when outside SBP65..280, DBP35..160 or pulse pressure<10; this plausibility safeguard can slightly change source moment/correlation matches and regression coefficients. BMI floor12 is a modeling safeguard, not a released dictionary bound; no independent weight/height is claimed.
ANALYSES: Primary suggested equal-weight OLS: SBP~1+age+female+(BMI/5), DBP~same; report BMI coefficients in mmHg per5kg/m^2. Pearson correlation of their two residual vectors is analysis3. Because generation includes nonlinear/sex-specific age means, also examine flexible age adjustment with age, (age-55)_+, age*female and (age-55)_+^2. Age/sex-adjusted associations are descriptive, not causal effects. Neither residual rho nor BMI associations validate the excluded population. No empirical cohort is postprocessed to force slopes/correlation.
